entries.subject: Schenk 2020 corrected image cube
entries.finding: Included as Monochrome: controlled, mapped original with numeric validity and processing history.

entries.subject: Schenk uumapZlimb.cub
entries.finding: Excluded from Elevation: the release labels it a limb profile in map form. Its README warns this separate product uses an older control network displaced by degrees. Sparse limb measurements cannot supply a surface elevation map.
entries.revisitWhen: A released Umbriel topographic reconstruction provides extended measured coverage registered to the selected mosaic; sparse limb values alone cannot fill that gap.

entries.subject: Schenk and Moore 2023
entries.finding: Supports native 4 km imaging and limited Umbriel topography; no complementary extended terrain raster qualified.

entries.subject: JPL legacy map catalog
entries.finding: Older display texture; no additional scientific meaning over the corrected original. Replaced rather than a duplicate dataset.
entries.revisitWhen: A controlled replacement provides useful observed detail or coverage beyond the selected corrected mosaic.

entries.subject: PDS Voyager imaging archive
entries.finding: Original frames require independent calibration, registration and mosaic preparation. No better ready registered Umbriel product qualified here.
entries.revisitWhen: A Umbriel observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Carbon oxide spectroscopy
entries.finding: Hemispheric spectra are scientifically useful but do not provide a qualified spatial composition raster for this dataset system.
entries.revisitWhen: A spatially resolved Umbriel measurement supplies original spectral or image samples with body-fixed coordinates and enough coverage to qualify a mapped dataset.

entries.subject: NASA press photographs and interior models
entries.finding: Disc photographs are not longitude/latitude maps; inferred interiors are not observed surface data. No fabricated color or interior dataset.
entries.revisitWhen: A Umbriel observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Wunda ring display-range trial
entries.finding: The narrower monochrome stretch clipped the bright Wunda ring and was rejected. The selected 0–1950 DN display range retains that feature while the original floating-point cube remains intact. This is not a physical reflectance scale.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet color frames
entries.finding: 3 GEOMED frames in 1 complete sets (16.9 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color dataset. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (1.0, 1.03); the archive calibration gives 0.948 and 1.010. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hapke law of Helfenstein and Veverka (1988), an open conference abstract (Lunar and Planetary Science XIX, 477). They fitted Hapke's 1986 equation to disc-resolved brightness in five Voyager clear-filter images at 10.4 to 142.9 degrees phase. Table I, disc-resolved row: w = 0.34, h = 0.06 (fixed at the whole-disc value), S(0) = 1.28, g = -0.18, roughness 28 degrees. The model here takes the opposition amplitude B0, so S(0) is converted with the authors' own definition, B0 = S(0)/(w P(0)), printed in their 1986 NASA summary on the Moon: B0 = 2.145. Flood-lit, the limb is 0.99 of the centre; the opposition surge puts the point under the Sun at 0.61 of that centre at 10 degrees phase, so frames with Shadows on are dimmer than the flood-lit view. It is second class: no emission range is printed, and the limit 84.6 degrees is derived here from the outermost pixel of the finest of the five frames (FDS 26840.04, 5.167 km per pixel). The authors' later summary in NASA TM-4130 fits whole-disc and disc-resolved data together (0.372, -0.235, 26 degrees) but prints no opposition surge values, so the abstract's complete row is used. Helfenstein, Veverka and Thomas (1988), the whole-disc fits of the five moons, could not be read.
entries.revisitWhen: The fitted emission range, or a fit of whole-disc and disc-resolved data together with its opposition surge values, is read in a paper.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the Hapke law of Helfenstein and Veverka (1988); Umbriel now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Surface map left edge after the raster lane change
entries.finding: The raster lane writes this map from 0° E, but surface-map.json still declared the retired atlas's 180° E left edge, so the globe, labels and status-bar longitude were half a turn from the imagery. Read through its georeferenced source, the prepared normal map correlates 0.87 from 0° E and -0.10 from 180° E. The declaration is now 0° E, and preparation refuses a declared edge the source contradicts.
